entities.title: Khufu and the Great Pyramid
entities.description: Khufu ruled Egypt during the Fourth Dynasty, succeeding his father Snefru. By then, royal pyramid building was already well established: Snefru had commissioned three enormous pyramids and developed the smooth-sided form we recognise today. Khufu took this further with the Great Pyramid at Giza, the largest pyramid in Egypt, built as his tomb. It was part of a wider complex of temples and a causeway, with planned cemeteries for officials nearby. That setting helps explain the society behind the monument. Power was concentrated around the king, and senior offices were often held by his relatives. Even in death, officials were placed close to the ruler whose authority had shaped their lives.
entities.note: Reign dates, not a lifespan or precise construction interval. This follows the Met’s chronology.
